bullets.title: NVDA: CEO Huang investigated over alleged Chinese spy affair; stock down ~5.6%
bullets.body: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's alleged romantic relationship with a woman identified as a Chinese intelligence asset who may have helped China evade export controls. The board stated no evidence of IP or national security compromise and expressed confidence in Huang remaining CEO, but the DoJ is now involved after Commerce transferred the Megaspeed probe. Stock fell ~$9.85 (5.6%) to $176.79; Aletheia Capital downgraded to Hold; Polymarket pricing 17% odds Huang exits by Dec 31.

bullets.title: NVDA: Multiple analysts maintain Buy/'Buy the Drop' despite CEO overhang; RBC $330 PT, MS Top Pick
bullets.body: RBC expects a 3-4% FQ3 beat and 2-4% FQ4 raise, citing robust GPU rental prices (GB300 +24% M/M, B200 +10% M/M) and hyperscaler capex strength; stock trades at 12x CY27E EPS vs. >50% discount to semi peers with $200B+ buyback support. Morgan Stanley's Joe Moore reiterates NVDA as Top Pick. Klein notes near-term selling pressure from the CEO probe but sees 7-8x CY28 PE as compelling entry for patient buyers; AMD at $450 is an alternative near-term.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley 'Buy the Drop' AI thesis: hyperscalers/EQIX/power unchanged; 2028 US DC shifts to 2029
bullets.body: MS argues markets overreacted to midterm results — ~20% of US data center projects (5GW) shift from 2028 to 2029, not cancellation. Hyperscaler capex unchanged at $1.6T/$1.8T in 2027/2028; 2029 US DC growth expected +38% YoY. High-conviction OW: AMZN, META, GOOGL, MSFT, NVDA, AVGO, EQIX, powered-shell providers (HUT, WULF), power/IPPs (BE, SEI, VST, TLN, CEG), optical (LITE, COHR, ANET), storage (STX, WDC). Value creation expected to shift from semis/infra toward software/AI adopters.

bullets.title: Citi downgrades US/Global/EU Tech to Neutral tactically; not dip-buying semis yet
bullets.body: Citi Global Equity Strategy cut US, Global, and EU Tech from Overweight to Neutral, citing positioning risks and desire for cleaner sentiment before re-rating. The desk is not yet a dip-buyer in semis/tech despite acknowledging intact AI demand fundamentals.

bullets.title: HBM/DRAM super-cycle: SK Hynix HBM4 yields 60%+; Samsung adding HBM for AMD/NVDA; Q1'27 price hike expected
bullets.body: SK Hynix achieved mid-60% HBM4 yields (industry-leading); Samsung will produce HBM base dies for AMD and Nvidia at its Texas fab. DRAM market entered a $200B super-cycle with spot-price premiums of 30-50% and shortages expected through 2027; new fabs not online until 2028. GPU rental prices also rising: B300 +14.46% M/M, B200 +15.35% M/M.

bullets.title: TTD: up 16.1% on 181% above-average volume ahead of post-close earnings
bullets.body: The Trade Desk surged 16.1% on unusually heavy volume (181% of average) ahead of its earnings report due after the close today, flagged by StreetAccount as a watchlist unusual-volume alert.

bullets.title: DKNG: Multiple downgrades; PT cut to $22 from $28 after Q3 miss and deferred profitability to 2028
bullets.body: Citi cut DKNG PT to $22 from $28 after Q3 miss; Q4 2026 and FY2027 guidance came in well below Street on a significant increase in Prophet investment, pushing the path to profitability to 2028. Stifel, UBS, and JPMorgan also downgraded the stock. UBS separately flagged a possible low-hold NFL Week 9 (13/14 favorites won, 93% favorite win rate).

bullets.title: AMD: Oppenheimer upgrades to Outperform, $600 PT; benefits from NVDA distraction and Intel CPU weakness
bullets.body: Oppenheimer upgraded AMD to Outperform from Perform with a $600 price target, citing NVDA's CEO controversy creating an opening and AMD's solid recent quarter with Intel CPU market share gains. Stock was up ~4.1% pre-market.

bullets.title: GOOGL: New TPU chip family accelerates; Federal Circuit invalidates Google wireless patent vs. Sonos
bullets.body: Google is launching four specialized TPU SKUs in 2026, including chips for confidential computing and AI agent security (8tx pairs with AMD CPU; 8i Max doubles compute density), with stock up ~2.5-3% on the news. Separately, the Federal Circuit summarily affirmed PTAB's invalidation of a Google wireless network patent asserted against Sonos.

bullets.title: META: CSO Dave Wehner departing for Fireworks AI; launching Muse AI assistant; expanding age verification
bullets.body: META Chief Strategy Officer Dave Wehner is leaving to become CFO of Fireworks AI. The company is launching its Muse AI assistant in the UK with retail partnerships and expanding Instagram age-verification technology globally as lawsuits mount over youth social media harms. Stock was up ~2.9% pre-market.

bullets.title: MRVL/LITE: Marvell to acquire Lumentum at 4.5x fixed exchange ratio
bullets.body: Marvell Technology agreed to purchase Lumentum at a fixed exchange ratio of 4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share, as flagged in the StreetAccount weekly M&A summary.

bullets.title: CHTR: Q3 misses; targeting $2B opex cuts; sell-side evenly split buy/hold/sell
bullets.body: Charter Q3 proforma EBITDA fell 4% YoY to $6.59B (missed) and revenue fell 2% to $16.51B; FCF declined to $674M from $1.62B. Management targets $2B annualized opex savings over 18 months plus >$1B Cox synergies. Street is evenly split (33%/33%/33% buy/hold/sell); avg PT $176.25; TD Cowen sees CMCSA M&A as a potential solution.

bullets.title: AFRM: Well-positioned vs. Warren 10% credit card rate cap; October reaccelerated to high-30% volume growth
bullets.body: JPM notes AFRM is differentiated from traditional card issuers (0% financing, no late fees, ~$250 avg transaction) and therefore less exposed to Senator Warren's proposed 10% APR cap. Management feedback was incrementally positive on agentic commerce and the Affirm Card (targeting 20M users vs. ~6M today); October volume growth reaccelerated to high-30% after a timing-related Q1 slowdown.

bullets.title: CRSP: Citi Buy, $90 PT; CTX310 Ph1b shows ~63% triglyceride reduction at Day 30 with clean safety profile
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on CRISPR Therapeutics with a $90 PT (80% upside from ~$50). AHA 2026 data from the CTX310 Phase 1b trial showed ~63% mean triglyceride reduction and ~65% ANGPTL3 reduction at Day 30 (N=10 sHTG patients) with no treatment-related SAEs or Grade 3+ AEs. The ANGPTL3 editing program is now CRSP's lead cardiovascular program after Novartis' HORIZON data weakened the lipoprotein(a) rationale.

bullets.title: DLR: Unusual bearish options activity (Put/Call 42.95) post-EVGR LOI color; +3.9% stock
bullets.body: Digital Realty Trust saw options volume 595% above average with an extremely bearish Put/Call ratio of 42.95 following EVGR LOI commentary, even as the stock was up 3.9%. DLR is also confirmed at Citi's Nareit REITworld meetings (Nov 17-18) and the Jefferies pre-NAREIT bus tour (Nov 16) in Atlanta.

bullets.title: BABA: Chip unit T-Head Semiconductor planning HK IPO to raise $2-3B
bullets.body: Alibaba's semiconductor unit T-Head Semiconductor is planning a Hong Kong IPO next year targeting $2-3B (HK$15.68-23.52B); Alibaba plans to reorganize T-Head with partial employee ownership before listing.

bullets.title: FOXA: Seaport Research upgrades to Buy, $76 PT (9% upside)
bullets.body: Seaport Research Partners' David Joyce upgraded Fox Corp to Buy from Neutral with a $76 price target, implying 9% upside from $69.88. FactSet consensus target is $81.56.

bullets.title: ADBE/DIS: Multi-year strategic alliance for AI-powered tools across Disney innovation labs, parks, and cruises
bullets.body: Adobe and Walt Disney announced a multi-year strategic alliance in which Adobe's AI tools and custom models will support concept exploration in Disney's innovation labs and parks/cruise development pipelines, helping teams develop ideas more quickly while protecting creator IP.

bullets.title: SHOP: Partner Program simplification flagged as catalyst; FWONK upgraded to Hold
bullets.body: Zach Goldberg's AM Attack flagged SHOP's simplification of its Partner Program around attribution as a potential positive catalyst. FWONK (Formula 1) was separately upgraded to Hold.

bullets.title: ORCL: DC permit delays create structural advantage; $20B financing removes overhang; FCF turns positive 2HFY28
bullets.body: Klein notes ORCL is better positioned than peers as data center permit tightening limits AI supply and benefits existing infrastructure holders — ORCL has 5 mega-sites under construction with permits secured and targets ~10GW capacity by FY28 from ~3GW in FY26. The $20B financing removes a major funding overhang; free cash flow expected to turn positive in 2HFY28. MSFT GPU capacity non-renewals allow ORCL to re-contract older GPUs at higher prices.
